questions.q: What does this lesson say the general career ladder from analyst to architect represents?
options: A general shape to expect, not a guaranteed timeline for any individual career
A strict, identical timeline that applies to every person in every company
A path that always takes exactly the same number of years for everyone
A sequence that must be followed in a fixed order with no exceptions
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that this is a general, descriptive shape — not a promise about how fast any individual's career will move.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the primary focus of the Governance Manager / Program Manager rung?
options: Running the governance program itself — stakeholder management, roadmaps, KPIs, and budget/resourcing conversations
Executing individual glossary entries and data quality checks
Designing enterprise metadata and catalog architecture across platforms
Reviewing job postings for entry-level candidates
questions.explain: The Manager rung is described as the shift from doing governance work to running the governance program itself, covering stakeholders, roadmaps, and budget.

questions.q: What does this lesson say actually changes between an Analyst and a Senior Analyst, beyond the title?
options: The shift from completing a clearly defined task correctly to deciding how to handle an ambiguous task with no existing instructions
Nothing changes at all between these two rungs
Senior Analysts no longer need to understand data quality
The Senior Analyst role requires no governance judgment whatsoever
questions.explain: The lesson frames the Analyst-to-Senior-Analyst shift as moving from executing defined tasks to exercising judgment on ambiguous ones.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the Data Governance Architect rung specifically takes longer to reach?
options: It requires both deep governance judgment and hands-on technical breadth across multiple platforms, built up over sustained, multi-year experience
Because architects are not required to know anything about governance
Because it is purely a management title with no technical component
Because the role can be reached immediately after finishing this course
questions.explain: The lesson explains the architect rung combines governance judgment with technical breadth across platforms like Purview, Fabric, Unity Catalog, Snowflake, Power BI, Azure, and AWS — a combination that takes years to build.

questions.q: Does this lesson present the ladder as a strictly linear, mandatory sequence every governance professional must follow?
options: No — it explicitly says movement isn't always linear, and some people stay happily at an earlier rung for a long career without pursuing the architect track
Yes — every governance professional must become an architect eventually
Yes — skipping the Manager rung is never possible under any circumstances
No — the ladder has no connection to real governance career paths at all
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states the ladder describes common shapes, not a mandatory sequence, and that staying at an earlier rung is a legitimate, common outcome.
